entities.name: Campylobacter jejuni
observations: Acute campylobacteriosis can follow untreated surface or stream-water exposure; typical incubation is about 2–5 days with fever, abdominal cramps, and watery diarrhea that may become bloody.
Among the listed options, this best matches acute bloody diarrhea with low-grade fever after camping and stream-water consumption.

entities.name: STEC O157:H7 infection
observations: Causes acute hemorrhagic colitis after contaminated food or water, typically with prominent crampy abdominal pain and absent or low-grade fever; it is the key alternative but is less favored here than Campylobacter.

entities.name: Infectious bloody diarrhea
observations: The remaining choices are less consistent with the combined exposure and presentation: protozoal causes are usually watery or prolonged, C. difficile generally follows antibiotics or healthcare exposure, and Vibrio parahaemolyticus follows seafood or seawater exposure.
